title: Constructible sheaves are finitely presented in the category of sheaves
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, and let $\mathcal F$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], an object of the category $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathcal I$ be a small filtered category, $i\mapsto\mathcal G_i$ a diagram $\mathcal I\to\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $(\mathcal G,(c_i)_i)$ a colimit of it in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then the canonical map

$$
 \theta_{\mathcal F}:\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G_i)\longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)
$$

(colimit of sets; on the $i$-th term $g\mapsto c_i\circ g$) is a bijection; equivalently, every morphism $\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ is $c_i\circ g$ for some $i$ and some $g:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G_i$, and if $c_i\circ g=c_{i'}\circ g'$ for $g:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G_i$, $g':\mathcal F\to\mathcal G_{i'}$, there are morphisms $\alpha:i\to k$, $\alpha':i'\to k$ of $\mathcal I$ with $\mathcal G(\alpha)\circ g=\mathcal G(\alpha')\circ g'$.
(*Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.73.8, Tag [09Z4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Z4).* Stacks states it for any Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ and also for sheaves of sets and of abelian groups; it is stated here for sheaves of modules over a finite $\Lambda$, the generality of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf].)

proof.text: *Reformulation.* Call an object $\mathcal P$ of $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ *finitely presentable* if for every small filtered $\mathcal I$, every diagram $D:\mathcal I\to\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and every colimit cocone $(L,(c_i))$ of $D$ the canonical map $\theta_{\mathcal P}:\varinjlim_i\mathrm{Hom}(\mathcal P,D(i))\to\mathrm{Hom}(\mathcal P,L)$ is bijective; this is the notion of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-colimit-finitely-presentable] for $\mathcal C=\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, whose Hom-sets are small. The lemma says that $\mathcal F$ is finitely presentable. The two clauses of the 'equivalently' are surjectivity and injectivity of $\theta_{\mathcal F}$ read through the description of the elements of a filtered colimit of sets [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise]: by clause (1) there every element of $\varinjlim_i\mathrm{Hom}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G_i)$ is the class of some $g:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G_i$, and $\theta_{\mathcal F}$ sends it to $c_i\circ g$, which gives surjectivity $\Leftrightarrow$ factorization; by clause (2) the classes of $g$ and $g'$ are equal iff there are $\alpha:i\to k$, $\alpha':i'\to k$ with $\mathcal G(\alpha)\circ g=\mathcal G(\alpha')\circ g'$, which gives injectivity $\Leftrightarrow$ agreement after refinement.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.73.8 (Tag 09Z4, label lemma-constructible-is-compact), proof, case of sheaves of modules

proof.text: *A finite presentation of $\mathcal F$* (Stacks: 'by Lemma 095N'). By [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-finite-presentation] ($X$ qcqs, $\Lambda$ finite, $\mathcal F$ constructible) there are affine objects $U_1,\dots,U_n$, $V_1,\dots,V_m$ of $X_{\Et}$ and an exact sequence $\mathcal P_1\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal P_0\xrightarrow{g}\mathcal F\to0$ in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ with $\mathcal P_0=\bigoplus_{i=1}^nj_{U_i!}\Lambda_{U_i}$, $\mathcal P_1=\bigoplus_{j=1}^mj_{V_j!}\Lambda_{V_j}$, where $j_{W!}\Lambda_W$ is the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the presheaf $\Lambda_X[h_W]:V\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\mathrm{Mor}(V,W)}\Lambda_X(V)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module]; $g$ is a cokernel of $f$. The finite direct sums are finite coproducts in the abelian category $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and a cokernel of $f$ is a colimit of the diagram $\mathcal P_1\rightrightarrows\mathcal P_0$ formed by $f$ and $0$ (a morphism $h:\mathcal P_0\to\mathcal T$ with $hf=h0=0$ is the same as one with $hf=0$).

source.place: Lemma 59.73.8 (Tag 09Z4), proof, second paragraph, citing Lemma 59.73.6 (Tag 095N)

proof.text: *$j_{U!}\Lambda_U$ is finitely presentable for $U$ an affine object* (Stacks: 'it suffices to prove the lemma for $h_U$ ... Recall that $\mathrm{Mor}(h_U,\mathcal G)=\mathcal G(U)$. Hence the result follows from Sites, Lemma 0738'). Let $U\to X$ be an object of $X_{\Et}$ with $U$ affine. Then $U$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: the morphism $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ between affine schemes is affine, hence quasi-compact and separated, in particular quasi-separated, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), which is what quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme means [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For every $\mathcal H\in\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ there are bijections $\mathrm{Hom}(j_{U!}\Lambda_U,\mathcal H)\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{PMod}(\Lambda_X)}(\Lambda_X[h_U],\mathcal H)\cong\mathcal H(U)$, the first by the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], the second $\beta\mapsto\beta_U(e_{\mathrm{id}_U})$ by [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module]; both are natural in $\mathcal H$, so the composite $\epsilon_{\mathcal H}$ satisfies $\epsilon_{\mathcal H'}(w\circ\beta)=w_U(\epsilon_{\mathcal H}(\beta))$ for $w:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H'$. Now let $(\mathcal G,(c_i))$ be a colimit of a filtered diagram $(\mathcal G_i)$. The bijections $\epsilon_{\mathcal G_i}$ are compatible with the transition maps (naturality for $\mathcal G(\alpha)$), so they induce a bijection $\bar\epsilon:\varinjlim_i\mathrm{Hom}(j_{U!}\Lambda_U,\mathcal G_i)\to\varinjlim_i\mathcal G_i(U)$ (its inverse is induced by the $\epsilon_{\mathcal G_i}^{-1}$), and naturality for $c_i$ gives $\epsilon_{\mathcal G}\circ\theta_{j_{U!}\Lambda_U}=\Psi\circ\bar\epsilon$, where $\Psi:\varinjlim_i\mathcal G_i(U)\to\mathcal G(U)$ is induced by the $(c_i)_U$ (both sides send the class of $\beta:j_{U!}\Lambda_U\to\mathcal G_i$ to $(c_i)_U(\epsilon_{\mathcal G_i}(\beta))$). $\Psi$ is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-qcqs-sections-filtered-colimit] ($U$ qcqs), so $\theta_{j_{U!}\Lambda_U}=\epsilon_{\mathcal G}^{-1}\circ\Psi\circ\bar\epsilon$ is bijective. (For modules, Stacks' $h_U$ is replaced by $j_{U!}\Lambda_U$, whose Hom into $\mathcal G$ is again $\mathcal G(U)$.)

source.place: Lemma 59.73.8 (Tag 09Z4), proof, first paragraph (sets: Mor(h_U,G)=G(U) and Sites, Lemma 7.17.7, Tag 0738), transferred to modules as the second paragraph says

proof.text: *Passing to the finite colimits* (Stacks: 'the result follows in the same way'). By step 3 every $j_{U_i!}\Lambda_{U_i}$ and every $j_{V_j!}\Lambda_{V_j}$ is finitely presentable. $\mathcal P_0$ and $\mathcal P_1$ are colimits of finite discrete diagrams of these objects (step 2), hence finitely presentable by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-colimit-finitely-presentable]. $(\mathcal F,g)$ is a colimit of the diagram $\mathcal P_1\rightrightarrows\mathcal P_0$ formed by $f$ and $0$ (step 2), a diagram over a finite category (two objects, four morphisms) with finitely presentable values, so $\mathcal F$ is finitely presentable by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-colimit-finitely-presentable] again. By step 1 this is the statement. (Concretely, the same conclusion is the diagram chase: $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathcal F,\mathcal H)=\ker(\mathrm{Hom}(\mathcal P_0,\mathcal H)\to\mathrm{Hom}(\mathcal P_1,\mathcal H))=\ker(\prod_i\mathcal H(U_i)\to\prod_j\mathcal H(V_j))$, and a filtered colimit of abelian groups commutes with finite products and kernels; the cited Mathlib leaf packages this.)

blueprint_proof_text:
Two recorded inputs are used. First, a constructible sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules is a finite colimit of representable sheaves $h_W$ with
$W\to X$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated (Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology,
Lemma 59.73.5, Tag [09Y9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09Y9), whose
proof argues by a finite stratification of $X$ and induction on the number of
strata). Second, for such a $W$ the sections $\mathcal
G(W)=\operatorname{Mor}(h_W,\mathcal G)$ of a sheaf commute with filtered
colimits of sheaves (Stacks Project, Sites, Lemma 7.17.7, Tag
[0738](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0738): a quasi-compact
quasi-separated object of a site is coherent). Colimits in the first variable
are computed on the presentation, and the two assertions of the statement are
respectively the existence and the uniqueness of the factorization, so the two
inputs give the bijection.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks 09Z4 (etale-cohomology.tex lemma-constructible-is-compact) and its inputs 09Y9 (sets), 095N (modules), 09YT (abelian) and Sites 0738. Statement restricted from Noetherian to finite Lambda and to sheaves of modules (the DAG's constructible-sheaf definition is for finite Lambda; the only user, lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaf-colimit-constructible, is for finite Lambda and modules); the 'equivalently' clause made precise. stmt_deps: def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes (complexes, unused) replaced by def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf, plus scheme conventions, module category and colimit. The blueprint proof cited 09Y9 (sheaves of sets, coequalizers of h_W) for modules; the Stacks proof for modules uses 095N (cokernel of finite sums of j_{U!}Lambda_U), which is followed here. Proof in 4 steps: reformulation (filtered colimits of sets, Mathlib leaf), presentation (new node 095N), j_{U!}Lambda_U finitely presentable via Hom = sections (free Yoneda leaf + sheafification) and new node for Sites 0738 on qcqs etale objects, finite colimits of finitely presentable objects (new Mathlib leaf CategoryTheory.isCardinalPresentable_of_isColimit at aleph_0). slopmaster2 has AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isFinitelyPresentable_of_isConstructibleSheaf (own sorry, WeilConjectures/ConstructibleSheaf/FinitePushforward.lean:94-97, docstring names this node) with IsNoetherianRing Lambda and finite stalks; node lean_audit left for the lead.
